Cosmological spectral background (Iν0​​)

Words: 284 Articles: 4
Cosmology OurBigBook.com
The cosmological spectral background is received radiant power per detector area, received frequency interval and solid angle, summed over a cosmological source population. Its intensity depends on emitted spectra, their cosmic evolution, the expansion history and absorption. A finite radial comoving distance alone does not guarantee a finite background when high-redshift sources are sampled at increasingly high emitted frequencies.

Cosmological bolometric background from conserved sources (F0​=cLn0​∫a(t)dt)

Words: 119 Articles: 1
Cosmological spectral background OurBigBook.com
Normalize the scale factor to a0​=1. Identical isotropic sources of bolometric luminosity L and conserved comoving number density n0​=a3n produce all-sky radiative flux F0​=cLn0​∫a(t)dt in a transparent FLRW metric. The source counts on an FLRW past light cone and cosmological flux dimming cancel the transverse shell-area factor. For arbitrary proper source density the expression is instead cL∫n(t)a(t)4dt. The intensity per solid angle is F0​/(4π). A detector of collecting area A receives power AF0​ under an all-sky effective-area convention.

Open dust bolometric background integral (F0​=4H0​(1−Ω0​)5/2cLn0​Ω02​​J(u0​))

Words: 56
Cosmological bolometric background from conserved sources OurBigBook.com
For an open matter-dominated Friedmann solution, put u=H0​1−Ω0​​τ, a=Ω0​(coshu−1)/[2(1−Ω0​)] and coshu0​=2/Ω0​−1. The cosmological bolometric background from conserved sources has J(u)=sinh(2u)/4−2sinhu+3u/2, since J′=(coshu−1)2 and dt=adu/[H0​1−Ω0​​]. At fixed H0​, the limit Ω0​→0 is cLn0​/(2H0​), whereas the Einstein-de Sitter universe gives 2cLn0​/(5H0​). Keeping the cosmic age fixed instead reverses this ordering: the two values are respectively cLn0​t0​/2 and 3cLn0​t0​/5.

Cosmological background intensity from comoving emissivity (Iν0​​=4πc​∫(1+z)H(z)ϵ(1+z)ν0​​(z)​dz)

Words: 113 Articles: 1
Cosmological spectral background OurBigBook.com
Let ϵνe​​(z) be the comoving spectral emissivity, namely total emitted spectral luminosity per comoving volume. In a homogeneous transparent FRW metric, a radial shell contributes its comoving volume times the cosmological spectral flux-density relation. Its transverse-area factors cancel, leaving the displayed integral. In a flat model this cancellation is explicit: dVc​=r2(c/H)dzdΩ, whereas Fν0​​=(1+z)Lνe​​/[4π(1+z)2r2]. Absorption inserts a transmission factor, and evolving sources are represented by the redshift dependence of ϵ.

Einstein-de Sitter spectral-background convergence criterion (α<3/2)

Words: 52
Cosmological background intensity from comoving emissivity OurBigBook.com
For nonevolving comoving number density n0​, identical spectra Lν​∝να, and no attenuation, the cosmological background intensity from comoving emissivity in an Einstein-de Sitter universe is proportional to ∫0∞​(1+z)α−5/2dz. The improper integral is finite exactly for α<3/2, with value 1/(3/2−α). Equality gives logarithmic divergence; larger α gives a power-law divergence. A formation epoch or a spectral break can regularize this idealized model.

Cosmological monopole problem

Words: 89 Articles: 1
Cosmology OurBigBook.com
The cosmological monopole problem is the excessive relic density of stable magnetic monopoles produced in some early-universe symmetry-breaking scenarios. Cosmic inflation dilutes their number density as a−3. Successful later reheating must also avoid recreating an excessive abundance.

Cosmological monopole problem OurBigBook.com
For a radiation-era transition at Ti​∼η, use Hi​=1.66g∗​​η2/mpl​ and initial number density ni​=Cn​Hi3​. Stable monopoles of mass CM​η redshift as nonrelativistic matter. With comoving entropy conservation,
ρM0​∼Cn​CM​(1.66)3g∗3/2​g∗s,i​g∗s,0​​mpl3​η4T03​​.
(1)
The fourth-power scale dependence makes even a small causal initial abundance incompatible with conventional high-scale grand unification unless inflation, later entropy production or efficient destruction reduces the relic population.

Structure formation

Words: 28
Cosmology OurBigBook.com
Structure formation is the growth of cosmological matter inhomogeneities into structures such as galaxies through gravitational instability and gas dynamics. Linear cosmological density perturbations describe the early, small-amplitude regime; nonlinear evolution is required once the density contrast becomes large.

Cosmological principle

Words: 160 Articles: 2
Cosmology OurBigBook.com
The cosmological principle assumes that the universe is statistically homogeneous and isotropic on sufficiently large spatial scales. It applies to a coarse-grained description, not to each galaxy or local void. Combined with the Copernican principle, cosmological isotropy around us supports a homogeneous description rather than a specially centred model. It motivates an FRW metric, whose expansion is governed by a few time-dependent quantities. Observations sample only a finite past light cone, so they support this hypothesis without proving global spatial homogeneity beyond the observed region.

Cosmological isotropy

Words: 45
Cosmological principle OurBigBook.com
Cosmological isotropy means that coarse-grained spatial observations or their statistics are unchanged by rotations about an observer. In an FRW metric it holds about every comoving location. cosmological isotropy about a single location is weaker than spatial homogeneity: a radially inhomogeneous model centred on that location can also have an isotropic sky.

Copernican principle

Words: 41
Cosmological principle OurBigBook.com
Our observer location is not specially privileged. In cosmology this assumption allows cosmological isotropy observed around us to be interpreted statistically as cosmological isotropy around other typical observers. It is an assumption about typicality, not a deduction from one observer's sky or from the Einstein field equations alone.

Cosmological particle freeze-out

Words: 318 Articles: 5
Cosmology OurBigBook.com
Decoupling of a particle abundance from chemical equilibrium when interactions become too slow compared with cosmic expansion. Pair annihilation can continue after equilibrium production is negligible, leaving a nonzero relic abundance.

Thermal relic (Y=n/s)

Words: 68
Cosmological particle freeze-out OurBigBook.com
A thermal relic is a surviving particle population whose earlier abundance was set by chemical thermal equilibrium with the cosmic plasma. After number-changing reactions cease and cosmic entropy is conserved, its comoving abundance is described by the yield Y=n/s. A relativistically decoupled species can retain an appreciable yield, whereas a species remaining in thermal equilibrium after becoming nonrelativistic is subject to Boltzmann suppression. Its later mass density, lifetime and momentum distribution determine its cosmological effects.

Thermalization temperature for a massless gauge mediator (Γ/H=αY2​mpl​/(1.66g∗​​T))

Words: 70
Cosmological particle freeze-out OurBigBook.com
A rate proportional to T competes with radiation-era expansion proportional to T2. The interaction-to-expansion ratio therefore grows as the universe cools, crossing unity near Teq​=αY2​mpl​/(1.66g∗​​). If a phase transition occurs at Tc​≫Teq​, this high-temperature interaction never establishes thermal equilibrium before the transition. Subsequent faster number-changing processes may still establish a thermal distribution; the initial state is not automatically Fermi-Dirac just because the particles are relativistic.

Mass-dependent fermion freeze-out (mnr​=1.66g∗​​αY4​mpl​​,TD​=mY​(mY​/mnr​)1/3)

Words: 127 Articles: 1
Cosmological particle freeze-out OurBigBook.com
In a radiation-dominated toy model with Γ=αY4​T5/mY4​, setting the interaction rate equal to the Hubble parameter gives the displayed decoupling scale. The transition TD​=mY​ defines mnr​. For smaller masses, xD​=mY​/TD​=(mnr​/mY​)1/3≫1. An instantaneous chemically equilibrated cosmological particle freeze-out estimate gives nY​/s=[45gY​/(2π2g∗s​)(2π)−3/2]xD3/2​e−xD​. This estimate presupposes number-changing thermal equilibrium, radiation domination and the assumed rate law, rather than following from elastic thermalization alone.

Thermal relic density bound for a tunable fermion (ρB​ρY​​=mB​mY​​YB​YY​​,Yi​=ni​/s)

Words: 69
Mass-dependent fermion freeze-out OurBigBook.com
For a stable nonrelativistic thermal relic, compare energy densities rather than number densities. If mY​=mnr​/x3 and YY​=Cx3/2e−x, its density relative to baryons is (Cmnr​/mB​YB​)x−3/2e−x. Requiring this ratio below an allowed dark-matter-to-baryon ratio R means x+23​logx≥log[Cmnr​/(RmB​YB​)]. With fixed rate parameters this excludes the weakly interacting large-mass branch, while the sufficiently Boltzmann-suppressed smaller-mass branch can satisfy the density bound. Heavy-boson decay baryogenesis (ϵ=(r−rˉ)/2)

Words: 133
Baryogenesis OurBigBook.com
Consider equal initial abundances of a heavy boson X and its antiparticle. Two decay channels with different baryon numbers, for example X→uu and X→dˉe+, have branching fractions r and 1−r. The conjugate channels have branching fractions rˉ and 1−rˉ. Their mean baryon numbers are r−1/3 and −rˉ+1/3, so each particle-antiparticle pair produces r−rˉ, or ϵ per decaying particle. Unequal branching fractions require CP violation; equal total decay widths are consistent with CPT symmetry. Baryon number cannot be assigned so that both channels conserve it. An initial abundance decaying outside thermal equilibrium, after inverse production becomes ineffective, can therefore generate a nonzero baryon asymmetry. At the microscopic level a decay-rate difference caused by CP violation requires interference of decay amplitudes with both a relative weak phase and an absorptive phase; complex couplings alone do not guarantee it. Subsequent baryon-number washout must be ineffective for the produced asymmetry to survive.

The cosmological constant problem is the unexplained smallness of the gravitationally observable vacuum energy compared with the contributions expected from quantum field theory. These observables probe different astrophysical environments and systematic errors.

Primordial non-Gaussianity is any departure of the primordial perturbations from Gaussian random fields. Cubic interactions generate a nonzero three-point correlation function at leading order.

Sunyaev-Zeldovich effect

Words: 218 Articles: 3
Cosmic microwave background OurBigBook.com
Hot Electrons in galaxy clusters scatter photons of the cosmic microwave background, producing a characteristic spectral distortion. The thermal contribution measures a line-of-sight integral of Electron pressure, whereas X-ray emission depends approximately on the integral of Electron density squared times a temperature-dependent emissivity. Combining the two with a geometrical model can constrain a cluster's physical size and hence its angular diameter distance. Temperature structure and departures from the assumed geometry introduce systematic uncertainty.

Eliminating ne​ and using dL​=(1+z)2dA​ yields the displayed angular diameter distance. A model for the density profile fixes its numerical coefficient. Clumping, nonsphericity and temperature structure can bias this distance because the two observables weight the gas differently.

In the nonrelativistic, single-scattering limit it has the spectrum of a small blackbody temperature change, unlike the thermal Sunyaev-Zeldovich effect.

The equivalent thermodynamic temperature perturbation has the displayed form, while the Rayleigh-Jeans law gives ΔT/T=−2y. The distortion changes sign at x≃3.830. This first-order expression assumes a small Compton y parameter and nonrelativistic thermal Electrons.

If the heated sound speed exceeds the escape-speed scale, the previous hydrostatic equilibrium is lost and a pressure-driven outflow removes gas. This particularly affects haloes whose virial temperatures are below the usual atomic cooling threshold and reduces their subsequent star formation.

Dark matter OurBigBook.com
If a dark matter particle of mass mχ​ radiates power ϵ independently of its neighbours, optically thin isotropic emission has volume emissivity j=ϵρ/mχ​. Its surface brightness is I=(4π)−1∫jdz and therefore traces the mass column rather than its square.

Weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP)

Words: 78
Dark matter OurBigBook.com
A weakly interacting massive particle is a massive dark-matter candidate whose interaction strength permits thermal production and later cosmological particle freeze-out. Its relic abundance depends on the annihilation rate and cosmological history, not on its mass alone. At nucleosynthesis temperatures a 50 GeV example is nonrelativistic: its equilibrium density is reduced by Boltzmann suppression, while an already frozen relic population need not follow the equilibrium density. Its effect on nucleosynthesis depends on whether the surviving energy density is appreciable or whether it injects reaction-altering products.

Cold dark matter (CDM)

Words: 21
Dark matter OurBigBook.com
Cold dark matter is nonrelativistic early enough that its primordial free-streaming length is small compared with the cosmological structures of interest.

Warm dark matter (WDM)

Words: 28
Dark matter OurBigBook.com
Warm dark matter has a primordial collisionless free streaming length large enough to suppress the formation of low-mass haloes, while remaining nonrelativistic early enough to cluster on galactic and larger scales.

Matter-radiation equality

Words: 54 Articles: 1
Cosmology OurBigBook.com
Matter-radiation equality is the epoch at which the background matter and radiation densities are equal. Its horizon wavenumber keq​ sets the turnover scale of the cold-dark-matter transfer function.

Matter-radiation equality scale (keq​)

Words: 25
Matter-radiation equality OurBigBook.com
The matter-radiation equality scale is the comoving horizon wavenumber at equality. Modes at larger wavenumber entered during radiation domination and had their matter growth suppressed.

Cosmic string

Words: 32
Cosmology OurBigBook.com
A cosmic string is a hypothetical one-dimensional topological defect formed by symmetry breaking in the early universe. A cosmic string network consists of many such defects and requires additional assumptions to infer an averaged equation of state.

Hubble's law (v=Hd)

Words: 23
Cosmology OurBigBook.com
Hubble's law relates recession velocity and distance in homogeneous cosmic expansion. The associated Hubble flow is the velocity field; peculiar velocities are deviations from that idealized expansion.

Comoving and proper distances

Words: 38
Cosmology OurBigBook.com
Comoving and proper distances are two cosmological distance conventions. For simultaneous radial separations in an FLRW model, proper distance equals the comoving radial distance multiplied by the scale factor at that cosmic time. A comoving coordinate remains fixed on an ideal comoving observer's worldline.

Age of the universe

Words: 32
Cosmology OurBigBook.com
The age of the universe is elapsed cosmic time since the early hot Big Bang phase, inferred within a cosmological model from expansion and matter-content measurements. The age of an FLRW universe is the corresponding model computation from its scale-factor evolution.

Non-Gaussianity

Words: 25
Cosmology OurBigBook.com
Non-Gaussianity means a departure from Gaussian statistics of a physical quantity or random field. Higher connected correlation functions describe such departures. Primordial non-Gaussianity concerns the initial cosmological perturbations.
